Anything found that is too large for a single iteration is written here as a user story and picked up on a later pass. Iterations already spent are recorded in `loop.completed` so a fresh session can resume without re-auditing.

userStories.title: Stop dating every static sitemap URL with the request date
userStories.description: As a search engine, I want <lastmod> to mean something, so that the dates on blog posts and guides are worth acting on.
acceptanceCriteria: renderSitemap emits <lastmod> only for entries that carry one
The 29 static marketing routes carry no <lastmod>
Blog posts and pSEO guides keep the real timestamp from their row
isoDate returns undefined instead of falling back to today
The Cloudflare Pages fallback sitemap carries no <lastmod> either
Unit tests cover the rendering, not just the source text
userStories.notes: Pure rendering moved to supabase/functions/generate-sitemap/render.ts so vitest can import it (index.ts imports the Supabase client from esm.sh and reads Deno.env, so it can only ever be asserted as text). Covered by src/lib/sitemap-render.test.ts, 9 tests. functions/sitemap.xml.ts lost all 29 `<lastmod>${today}</lastmod>` lines and the now-unused `today`. STATIC_ENTRIES stayed in index.ts because five other tests read that file as text for the route list.

userStories.title: A missing blog slug served the homepage head on an indexable page
userStories.description: As a search engine, I want a dead /blog/* URL to say it is a dead URL, so that it is not indexed as a thin duplicate that canonicalises to the homepage.
acceptanceCriteria: The not-found branch of BlogPost declares a head of its own
It sets robots noindex, follow
It leaves no canonical standing, so the homepage canonical in index.html does not apply to it
It carries a title that is not the homepage's
Tests cover all four
userStories.notes: src/pages/BlogPost.tsx's `if (!post)` branch rendered a 404 body with no Helmet at all. Because index.html is the SPA fallback document, its data-rh defaults describe the homepage, so every deleted post, draft, typo and stale inbound link under /blog/ answered 200 with the homepage title, the homepage description and <link rel="canonical" href="https://tryeatpal.com/">. Fixed by mirroring NotFoundState in src/pages/pseo/PseoPage.tsx, which already had this right. Covered by src/pages/BlogPost.notFound.test.tsx, 4 tests.

userStories.title: The ARFID cluster had no sitewide link
userStories.description: As a search engine, I want the site's own links to say which pages matter, so that the cluster closest to what EatPal is for is not the one nothing points at.
acceptanceCriteria: All four /arfid/* pages are linked from the sitewide footer
The footer's existing layout absorbs it without reflowing
A test fails if a future ARFID page is added without a footer link
userStories.notes: /arfid/what-is-arfid, /arfid/arfid-vs-picky-eating and /arfid/arfid-in-adults were reachable from /picky-eater-quiz alone, and /arfid/safe-foods-list from /budget-calculator alone. The four pages cross-link each other, which makes them a closed loop rather than a cluster something points into. Meanwhile the footer already carried all five /picky-eater/* pages, /guides and /compare, each added after exactly this problem was found there. The nav is lg:grid-cols-6 and had five columns, so the ARFID column filled a reserved slot. Pinned by a new assertion in src/lib/arfid-content.test.ts, matching the one /compare has.

userStories.title: /guides claimed noindex guides as the members of its collection
userStories.description: As a search engine, I want a CollectionPage to name pages the site wants indexed, so that its ItemList is not contradicted by the robots tag on the pages it names.
acceptanceCriteria: The CollectionPage ItemList enumerates only guides at or below MAX_INDEXABLE_TIER
numberOfItems counts the same set
The page itself still lists every published guide for readers
Tests cover the split
userStories.notes: GuidesIndex selected slug, title, meta_description and page_type -- no tier -- so its CollectionPage/ItemList named whatever came back, including every guide above MAX_INDEXABLE_TIER that PseoPage marks noindex, follow. Listing those for readers is the documented intent (see src/lib/pseo/indexability.ts) and is unchanged; claiming them in schema is a different act, and numberOfItems was counting them too. GuidesIndex is the fourth surface that has to agree with MAX_INDEXABLE_TIER and the only one that can import the rule instead of restating it, which it now does. src/pages/pseo/GuidesIndex.schema.test.tsx, 4 tests.

userStories.title: Blog posts claimed they had never been edited
userStories.description: As a search engine, I want the page and the sitemap to agree about when a post last changed, so that the freshness signal on updated posts is not thrown away.
acceptanceCriteria: BlogPost fetches blog_posts.updated_at
ArticleSchema receives dateModified instead of falling back to datePublished
SEOHead receives datePublished and dateModified, so article:published_time and article:modified_time are emitted
A row whose updated_at precedes publication does not backdate the post
An absent or unparseable updated_at falls back to publication
Tests cover each case
userStories.notes: BlogPost's query never selected updated_at, so ArticleSchema was passed no dateModified and fell back to datePublished -- every post asserting it had not been touched since the day it went up -- and SEOHead was passed no dates at all, so neither article:published_time nor article:modified_time was emitted. The sitemap has been submitting isoDate(updated_at) for these same rows all along, so the site was contradicting itself: the sitemap saying a post changed last week, the page saying it never changed. lastEditedAt compares the two timestamps rather than trusting the column, because a row touched by a migration before its publish date is bookkeeping, not an edit. src/pages/BlogPost.freshness.test.tsx, 6 tests. Also lowered .ci/lint-baseline.txt from 1144 to 1143, the win from deleting generate-sitemap.js in iteration 5.

userStories.title: /authors: confirm whether it still self-noindexes (it does not)
userStories.description: As a site owner, I want the sitemap to stop advertising a URL that serves noindex, so that Search Console stops reporting 'Submitted URL marked noindex' and the E-E-A-T page either counts or is withdrawn.
acceptanceCriteria: Establish whether the page still sets noindex (it does not)
The sitemap's comment about /authors matches what the page actually does
The test carve-out comment matches too
No fabricated author rows
userStories.notes: Closed as already fixed, in iteration 2. src/pages/Authors.tsx no longer noindexes on an empty roster: a later pass replaced the credentials framing with an editorial-standards statement that holds whether or not blog_authors has rows, and the page is indexable unconditionally. Only the warnings were stale, and both now say so -- the STATIC_ENTRIES comment in supabase/functions/generate-sitemap/index.ts and the carve-out comment in src/lib/comparison-discovery.test.ts. Left as written, they would have talked someone into pulling a good URL out of the sitemap.

userStories.title: scripts/generate-sitemap.js is TypeScript in a .js file and cannot run
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want one sitemap generator, so that nobody reaches for the broken second one.
acceptanceCriteria: `node scripts/generate-sitemap.js` either runs or the file is gone
If kept, it agrees with supabase/functions/generate-sitemap on routes, retired slugs and the tier ceiling
Nothing in package.json or CI references a generator that does not exist
userStories.notes: Deleted in iteration 5. Nothing referenced it, and it could never have run: TypeScript interfaces in a .js file, so node threw a SyntaxError before the first statement. Had it run it would have written /recipes/<id> URLs for a route that only exists behind auth, plus a sitemap-index.xml pointing at a sitemap-dynamic.xml nothing serves. scripts/README.md now says where the real sitemap comes from, and documents/variables.md's two rows for VITE_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY under Scripts were repointed at scripts/prerender.mjs, which is what actually reads them (lines 193-198).

userStories.title: Edge-function tests: check whether they run (they do)
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the SEO logic that lives in supabase/functions to be covered by the suite, so that a change there is not shipped on inspection alone.
acceptanceCriteria: Establish whether supabase/functions tests run anywhere (they do, under deno test in ci.yml)
Establish whether vitest could run them (it cannot, they are Deno tests importing over https)
Record the residual risk: ci.yml lists the six paths by hand
userStories.notes: Closed as a false finding, in iteration 4. The six files under supabase/functions/_shared are Deno tests -- Deno.test, asserts from deno.land/std -- and ci.yml runs every one of them by name in a denoland/setup-deno job (lines 460-517). Widening vitest's include is the wrong fix and does not work anyway: all six fail collection under Node with "Only URLs with a scheme in: file and data are supported", because they import over https. Verified separately that the vitest suite itself is green: 3559 passing, 3 skipped, 240 files. One real gap remains and is not SEO: ci.yml enumerates those six paths by hand, so a seventh Deno test added tomorrow would never run. Worth a `deno test` glob, in some other loop.

userStories.title: Reconsider changefreq and priority in the sitemap
userStories.description: As a search engine, I want a sitemap that carries only fields I use, so that the file is smaller and says nothing misleading.
acceptanceCriteria: Establish whether Bing and the AI crawlers named in robots.txt read either field before removing them
If removed, the fallback sitemap and the tests that count fields follow
userStories.notes: Google has stated it ignores both. Lower value than SEO-002/003/004 and needs the Bing question answered first, so it sits at the bottom until the loop runs out of higher-value work.

userStories.title: Crashed routes were indexable 200s wearing the homepage head
userStories.description: As a search engine, I want an error state to say it is one, so that a crash on /pricing is not indexed as the homepage.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit the slug and data-driven pages for a soft 404 with no head
RouteErrorBoundary's fallback declares noindex, and clears it when the route recovers
The full-page boundary does the same
A single failed widget does NOT noindex the page around it
The mechanism works above <HelmetProvider>, where both global boundaries sit
userStories.notes: The audit came back clean on the pages it was written for: ComparisonPage, MealIdeasPage and ArfidPage all render <NotFound /> on an unknown slug, and the three /*/results pages, /api/docs, /join and /share already noindex. Blog, GuidesIndex and Authors render their own head unconditionally and are index pages with a purpose independent of their rows. What the audit did turn up sits a level higher: every route in src/App.tsx is wrapped in RouteErrorBoundary, whose fallback had no head at all, so a live crash -- a chunk 404 in the minutes after a deploy is the likely one -- served 'This page encountered an error' as an indexable 200 under the homepage title and canonical. Fixed with src/components/NoIndexOnError.tsx, a DOM write rather than a Helmet because both global boundaries sit above HelmetProvider and a Helmet there throws. scripts/prerender.mjs already refused to freeze an error state into static HTML (see its 'inherited the shell head' checks), so build time was covered and runtime was not. 7 tests.

userStories.title: Blog post breadcrumbs use relative URLs, which schema.org rejects
userStories.description: As a search engine, I want BreadcrumbList item values to be absolute URLs, so that the breadcrumb rich result is not discarded.
acceptanceCriteria: Every BreadcrumbList item is an absolute https://tryeatpal.com URL
Establish whether BreadcrumbSchema should absolutise defensively or every caller should pass absolute URLs
Audit all BreadcrumbNavigation and BreadcrumbSchema callers, not just BlogPost
A test fails if a relative item reaches the schema
userStories.notes: Found while inspecting the rendered head in iteration 6. A blog post emits itemListElement with item values of "/" and "/blog". ArfidPage passes absolute URLs to BreadcrumbSchema directly, so the two callers disagree and BlogPost is the wrong one. Needs a sweep of every caller plus a decision about where the absolutising belongs, which is more than the remainder of this iteration.
